# Tailwind Component Library Builder Skill

**Category:** Tech Skills > Frontend > Tailwind CSS

## Purpose

Provides specialized knowledge, step-by-step procedures, and quality standards for Tailwind Component Library Builder operations using Tailwind CSS technology. This skill encapsulates technology-specific best practices, design patterns, performance optimization techniques, and production-grade implementation guidance for Tailwind CSS within Frontend development.

## When to Use

- When building a shared component library with Tailwind CSS
- When implementing component variants with class-variance-authority
- When creating design system components with consistent styling
- When Tailwind CSS-specific technical expertise is required
- When best practices for Tailwind CSS technology stack must be applied
- When production-grade Tailwind CSS implementation guidance is needed

## Capabilities

- Build component variants with class-variance-authority (CVA)
- Implement compound variants for complex state combinations
- Create tailwind-merge safe class composition
- Design component tokens for customization
- Document component API with Storybook integration

## Procedure

1. Design component API with variant options
2. Implement variants with CVA and tailwind-merge
3. Create compound variants for state combinations
4. Add Storybook stories for documentation
5. Test visual consistency with screenshot testing
6. Package library for distribution

## Technology Standards

| Standard / Best Practice | Relevance |
|--------------------------|-----------|
| **CVA** | Class-variance-authority for variant management |
| **tailwind-merge** | Intelligent class merging for overrides |
| **Storybook** | Component documentation and visual testing |

## Anti-Hallucination Rules

- Do not assume CVA API without checking the installed version
- Verify tailwind-merge compatibility with Tailwind version
- Do not fabricate version numbers, API endpoints, or library names
- Always cite the specific documentation, RFC, or standard being referenced
- If technology-specific data is unavailable, explicitly state the gap and request clarification
- Never assume features exist in a specific version without verification

## Quality Checks

- Variants cover all required states
- Class composition does not produce conflicts
- Components render consistently across browsers
- All code examples must be syntactically valid and tested
- Cross-reference findings against official documentation
- Flag any assumptions made during analysis with explicit markers
- Validate all performance claims with reproducible benchmarks
- Ensure all recommendations follow Tailwind CSS community best practices
